name: Fable Unconstrained
strategy: Dual-momentum: long 6-month sector/asset leaders that are NOT in a sharp 1-month correction (energy, healthcare, a trimmed financials sleeve, one surviving cyber name), a small unlevered BTC mean-reversion sleeve now with a take-profit, no leverage, 47% cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: This is a resize, not a rebuild: XLE, FTNT and BTC weights are unchanged and only XLF/XLV move (a 5-point shift, ~2-4bps of friction). What changed: (1) the Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 9/16 with 16 of 18 policymakers projecting another hike, the 10y touched 5% (highest since 2007), August CPI is 3.4% while the Conference Board LEI unexpectedly fell and industrial production was flat - a stagflation-lite tape that argues for keeping the 47% cash sleeve at 4% rather than deploying it. (2) Financials cracked: after BofA's Moynihan guided Q3 IB fees at least 10% below consensus and flat trading revenue on 9/14, GS and BAC fell ~8% on the week and XLF had its worst week since March. XLF still sits ~8% above its 50-day (55.82 vs 51.80) so the 6-month momentum signal is intact and the 1-month drawdown (-4.7% from the 58.60 high) is not yet 'sharp' by my rule, but the catalyst is a street-wide Q3 guide-down into earnings season, so I cut it from 8 to 5 rather than wait for the stop. (3) Healthcare is the sector where relative strength is improving (XLV +1.5% over the five sessions into the FOMC, sector-rotation work flagging it as moving from cooling-off to early accumulation while staples lose support), so the 3 points move from XLF to XLV. (4) BTC bounced from ~$75k after the CLARITY Act cloture vote failed 50-49 on 9/15 to ~$81k on Friday (+5.85% in one day); it is up 6% on my fill but down roughly a third year-on-year, so this remains a mean-reversion sleeve, not a momentum leg, and the Senate failure removed the main 2026 legislative catalyst. I am adding a +15% take-profit so the sleeve books the bounce instead of hoping for a trend. (5) Tech is the second-best sector YTD but the SOX fell as much as 29% from its June peak and AI names were still being sold in mid-September (the cyber rally on 9/14 was explicitly a rotation out of AI stocks), so it fails the 'not in a sharp 1-month correction' filter and stays out; I will revisit after Micron on 9/23 and core PCE on 9/24. Stops on the unchanged legs stay as they were.

positions.thesis: Unchanged at 17%. Energy is the top S&P sector YTD (+47.7%) and the strongest 6-month momentum asset in the universe. The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since late February, the East-West pipeline was shut on 9/11, and the IEA calls it the largest supply disruption in oil-market history; WTI is $95.71 even after three down sessions and Brent crossed $100 this month. XLE marked 64.31 on 9/18 vs my 64.03 fill. Oil pulling back on ceasefire hopes is the risk, which is what the 12% stop is for; I am not adding because 17% is already the largest leg and the last three sessions were down.

Unchanged at 12%. FTNT jumped 9% on 9/14 to within ~2% of its 52-week high as cybersecurity re-rated on the thesis that securing autonomous AI agents is a prerequisite for enterprise AI adoption (ZS +16.5%, CRWD/PANW +11-12% the same day); Fortinet was named a Leader and highest on Ability to Execute in the 9/10 Gartner Hybrid Mesh Firewall MQ and carries a Zacks #1. It has given back ~1% since my 171.77 fill (168.60 on 9/18) which is normal digestion after a 9% gap; the 12% stop handles the case where Bernstein's 'top' call on the group is right. It stays the single-name momentum leg.

Raised from 10 to 13, taking the 3 points from XLF. Healthcare is where relative strength is turning: XLV gained ~1.5% over the five sessions into the 9/16 FOMC and sector-rotation trackers moved it from 'cooling off' to 'early accumulation' while consumer staples lost support, so it is the defensive sector that is actually being bought rather than sold into a 5% 10-year. It is a two-year laggard with room to mean-revert if the LEI decline turns into a growth scare, and it marked 168.39 vs my 167.77 fill. The 10% stop stays; UNH weakness is the main drag inside the ETF.

Cut from 8 to 5. The 6-month signal is still on (XLF 55.82 vs 50-day 51.80 and 200-day 51.64, 52-week range 47.67-58.60) so I am not exiting, but the week's -2%+ was the worst since March on a street-wide guide-down: BofA said Q3 IB fees fall at least 10% and trading is flat, GS and BAC dropped ~8% on the week, and the group is now credit- and yield-sensitive with the 10-year at 5%. A momentum leg whose next catalyst (Q3 bank earnings in mid-October) has just been pre-announced weak deserves a smaller weight, not a bigger stop. The 10% stop stays as the exit if the 1-month correction becomes sharp.

Unchanged at 6%, now with a +15% take-profit added. This is a mean-reversion sleeve, not momentum: BTC is roughly a third below where it was a year ago, and the CLARITY Act's 50-49 cloture failure on 9/15 ended the market-structure bill for 2026. The sleeve is working (fill 76,150, mark 80,901, +6.2%) after Friday's +5.85% to ~$81k as yields and oil eased. A mean-reversion trade should sell the bounce: the TP at ~$87.6k (+15%) books it at the prior consolidation, the 12% stop at ~$67k limits the downside if the post-CLARITY selloff resumes. No leverage, no perp funding.
